cases.title: RBD filter — on one Multi-City leg only

rows.label: Reason
rows.value: Search does nothing on both branches when an RBD is set on leg 1 only: no request is sent and no message is shown (seen 2 times per branch). Control checks: no RBD on any leg → search runs; RBD on both legs → search runs; RBD on leg 2 only → no request.

assertions.assertion: A1 — Result set not empty
assertions.actual: No search request sent on either branch (waited 300 s, then retried once with network capture: 0 requests, 0 console messages, 0 UI messages)

assertions.assertion: A2 — Every leg 1 segment RBD = Q
assertions.actual: Not evaluable — no results

assertions.assertion: A3 — Same combinations on both branches
assertions.actual: Same outcome on both branches: search silently not submitted

assertions.assertion: A4 — Leg 2 RBDs, Integration vs Direct
assertions.actual: Not evaluable — no results

items: Confirmed defects: DEF-01 (Premium ignored on Integration, High), DEF-02 (First ignored on Integration, High), DEF-08 (Multi-City partial RBD blocks search, both, Medium — reproduced).
Parity difference, needs business clarification: DEF-03 — Direct returns only Integration’s lowest-priced option per flight (109/109 flights); both send isUpSelling=false.
Parity difference + probable result limit: DEF-04 — Integration exactly 200 offers in 4 searches; CAI⇄JED Direct 262 vs Integration 200.
Observations: DEF-05 cabin naming, baggage wording, TC-001 reload. Needs clarification: DEF-06. Not reproducible: DEF-07.
Withdrawn: 5 Emirates Economy Flex options only on Direct (round-trip) — same fares, brand labelled per leg differently.
Round-trip fare-option matching by brand label is not reliable; counts reported, individual one-side options not claimed.
